location.mountain: Highest tea district on the island

description.short: The palest and most delicate Ceylon tea — the 'Champagne of Ceylon', cultivated on the highest alpine peaks of the island
description.overview: Grown at the highest altitudes in Sri Lanka under cool temperatures reminiscent of an English summer — yielding a remarkably bright, pale golden infusion that defies the stereotypical brisk strength of Ceylon tea.
description.leaf: Delicate, fine twisted light brownish leaves with greenish flecks
description.aroma: Ethereal, floral, with a crisp citrus and fresh blossom bouquet
description.taste: Delicate, refined, airy floral sweetness with minimal astringency
description.processing: Plucking → withering → orthodox rolling → light-to-medium oxidation → drying

history.origin: Founded by British colonial administrators in the 19th century as a high-altitude hill station reminiscent of England's cool climate, earning the moniker 'Little England'.
history.development: The brisk mountain climate was ideal not only for respite from tropical heat, but for producing an extraordinarily refined tea.
history.modern: Today Nuwara Eliya is celebrated as Sri Lanka's premier luxury single-origin terroir, often likened in elegance to Darjeeling despite botanical differences.
interestingFacts: Dubbed the 'Champagne of Ceylon', highlighting its rank as the most delicate and prestigious tea of Sri Lanka.
Nuwara Eliya retains striking British colonial Tudor-style architecture, combining historic tourism with verdant mountain tea estates.
